name: grace
why: An old-school scientific plotting tool with a long lineage, a close call for a catalogue about odd old environments.

brief.what_it_is: Grace is a WYSIWYG 2D plotting tool for the X Window System and Motif, meaning you build graphs by pointing and clicking and see the result as you edit it. The homepage says it runs on practically any Unix-like OS and has been ported to VMS, OS/2, and Windows, with some functionality possibly missing on the ports. Input is mainly text data files and 1D netCDF files, plus data you type or compute inside the program. Output is publication-style plots exported as vector graphics (EPS, PDF, MIF, SVG) or bitmaps (PNG, PNM, JPEG). It also does curve fitting, FFT, integration, splines, and similar analysis, and has a built-in programming language.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Grace as a descendant of ACE/gr, also known as Xmgr, and aims at publication-quality scientific plots with precise control over graph features.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals beyond saying it has a built-in programming language, math functions that operate on whole arrays, and dynamically loadable C/Fortran modules for user-defined fitting functions and extensions. Type1 fonts are rasterized device-independently, with anti-aliasing, ligatures, and kerning. Everything can be controlled by external programs.
brief.install_notes: The homepage does not give installation steps. Software is downloaded from https://plasma-gate.weizmann.ac.il/pub/grace/, which has src/, patches/, contrib/, aux/, and README.packages, plus daily mirrors in Germany (ftp.fu-berlin.de) and Japan (ftp.u-aizu.ac.jp). Building from source is the implied route, but I did not read the README files in that directory. Package-manager executables (convcal, fdf2fit, gracebat, grconvert, xmgrace) were listed in the brew metadata, not in anything I read.
brief.standout: It is a 1990s-era X/Motif plotting program that is still listed with a full feature set: curve fitting with constraints and user-loadable C/Fortran modules, and Type1 font rendering with kerning. Many scientists still use it, which is unusual for something this old.
brief.status: Quiet. The download directory's src/ folder was last modified 2015-02-15, the COPYRIGHT file 2008-05-21, and the MIRRORS file 2008-07-29. The homepage has no release date or version number, and I did not check a Changes page. This is a judgement from directory timestamps, not a confirmed last-release date.
brief.caveats: The Motif/X11 interface means a graphical X environment is needed, and the Windows and VMS ports may lack some features, per the homepage. The homepage names a license page, but I did not fetch it, so I cannot say what the license is. The homepage's links are named in text without URLs, so I could not follow the User's Guide, Tutorial, or FAQ. The brew description calls it an 'old-school' tool, and the scout notes say it is a close call for a catalogue about odd old environments.
